text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Eviction spike on KV prefix cache in prod-us-east-1. Error rate for affected requests up to 4.2% (baseline 0.05%). Top symptom: correctness failures (stale reads) for a small set of tenant traffic. Auto-mitigation triggered: soft-bypass for some prefixes. Paging oncall: @Alex (oncall)

Alex (oncall): seen it, looking. Bringing context: started ~09:13 UTC, correlates with recent prefetch rollout (canary) + upstream burst of unusual short-lived keys.

Raj: any customer-facing errors yet?

Maya: quick check -> SLO alarms for 3 tenants hit error budget. Two are internal test tenants, one is real-prod tenant (tid: T-4271) experiencing occasional 5xx / model response mismatch.

Sam (sre): logs show repeated KV cache evictions with key churn. eviction_rate per-shard jumped x15. We have a backlog of prefix invalidation ops causing contention. Sample log: ```
[2024-06-05T09:14:02Z] shard-12 evict key=prefix:abcd ttl=0 reason=churn
[2024-06-05T09:14:03Z] read fallback -> origin for prefix:abcd status=200 source=backend
[2024-06-05T09:14:04Z] correctness-verify failed for tid=T-4271 key=prefix:abcd
```

Lia: initial impact assessment: ~0.03% of total traffic but concentrated on low-latency endpoints for tenant T-4271 -> visible in their API logs as elevated error spikes and doubled p95. Customer success already on standby.

Kevin: mitigation options we discussed: 1) global prefix bypass (reduces risk but increases origin load) 2) targeted prefix bypass for hot prefixes 3) reduce prefetch/prefill aggressiveness 4) apply tenant-level quota/rate-limit to smooth bursts 5) tune eviction smoothing (increase buffer window).

Alex (oncall): propose stepwise approach to avoid overload: first apply targeted bypass for the offending prefixes + trim tenant QPS for T-4271 to limit correctness surface. If origin load stays healthy, re-enable per-tenant caching with higher smoothing.

Maya: +1. I'll run targeted bypass for top 10 hot prefixes and lower prefetch factor by 50% for canary.

Sam (sre): I'll prepare a quick quota trim for T-4271 and open a temporary rate-limit rule. Suggested commands: ```bash
# targeted prefix bypass via control plane
curl -X POST https://control-plane.prod/reconcile/cache/bypass 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' 
  -d '{"scope":"prefix","values":["prefix:abcd","prefix:ef12", "prefix:9f00"],"reason":"eviction-surge-correctness-bypass"}'

# tenant quota trim (token-bucket)
curl -X POST https://control-plane.prod/config/tenant/T-4271/quota 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' 
  -d '{"qps": 0.6, "burst": 40, "reason":"live-mitigation-1745001234"}'
```

Raj: before we do that, what is origin capacity headroom? If we bypass we'll push traffic to backend model servers.

Kevin: current origin CPU is at 48% and model queue depth is nominal. We have ~2.5x headroom for this expected bypass if we only target a few prefixes. But global bypass may be risky.

Lia: Customer comms note: Contact CS to warn T-4271 about temporary throttling and that correctness incidents may persist for a short window. I'll draft a blunt but concise message.

Maya: executing targeted bypass now. Patching prefetch config to reduce aggressive fill. ```bash
# lower prefetch multiplier for canary group
curl -X PATCH https://control-plane.prod/config/prefetch 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' 
  -d '{"multiplier":0.5, "scope":"canary"}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: cache-bypass-service v2.4.1 -> prod (canary)

Alex (oncall): Sam, proceed with tenant quota trim once bypass confirms no spike. Keep me posted. Lia, loop CS.

Sam (sre): applied tenant trim at 09:18 UTC. Rule id: qtrim-1745001234. Quick check: CPU/queue stable. No immediate origin errors.

Maya: bypass rollout confirms (3/3 canary hosts): hotkey bypass in place for listed prefixes. Observed immediate drop in correctness verify failures for those keys. Metrics: correctness-fails down from 4.2% -> 1.1% in 2m.

Raj: nice. Any regression in latency?

Kevin: small p50 increase (~12ms) for the affected paths; p95 improved overall for T-4271. Acceptable tradeoff.

Lia: CS notified customer and scheduled a callback in 30m. Message includes ETA for rollback plan.

Alex (oncall): next steps: 1) keep bypass + quota trim for 30m observation window 2) apply eviction smoothing change if we still see churn 3) prepare a safe plan to re-enable cache per-tenant with adjusted smoothing and reduced prefetch multiplier 4) if origin shows rising load, plan to incrementally re-enable cache or add capacity.

Maya: prepping smoothing change (increase eviction smoothing window from 100ms -> 500ms). Will stage to canary. Command: ```bash
PATCH /config/cache/eviction HTTP/1.1
Host: control-plane.prod
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN
Content-Type: application/json

{"smoothing_ms":500, "scope":"canary", "reason":"reduce-eviction-churn-1745001234"}
```

Sam (sre): applying to canary now. Monitoring metrics.

deploy-bot: config applied to canary (eviction.smoothing=500ms)

Maya: after smoothing change, eviction_rate per-shard trending back toward baseline over 6m. Correctness failures now ~0.2% and trending down.

Alex (oncall): good. Prepare to start rollback sequence: re-enable per-tenant caching for T-4271 with adjusted smoothing and keep prefetch multiplier low for 1 hour before full ramp. Lia, please confirm wording for CS update: summary, mitigations applied, expected next steps.

Lia: Draft: "We applied targeted cache bypass for hot prefixes and temporarily trimmed your QPS to stabilize correctness. We also tuned eviction smoothing and reduced prefetch. Expect improved stability within 30–60 minutes. We'll follow up when full cache reinstated." Approve?

Raj: approve. Also add "no customer data was exposed" line.

Lia: added. Sending now.

Maya: initiating reinstatement for per-tenant caching on T-4271 (canary hosts) with new smoothing. Command: ```bash
POST /reconcile/cache/enable 
{"scope":"tenant","tenant_id":"T-4271","smoothing_ms":500 }
```

Sam (sre): reinstatement success on canary -> monitoring. No correctness regressions observed. origin qps still stable.

Alex (oncall): After 45m observation, metrics stable. Recommend full rollout of smoothing and keep prefetch multiplier at 0.5 for 1 hour then gradually ramp. Remove tenant quota trim after 60m.

Maya: scheduled quota trim removal at 10:20 UTC. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: action logged: incident-1745001234 mitigation steps recorded in incident tracker.

Alex (oncall): handing off to Raj for next watch. Summary for handoff: targeted prefix bypass + tenant qtrim applied, eviction smoothing increased to 500ms, prefetch multiplier lowered to 0.5 for canary -> will be ramped later. Customer impacted: T-4271 saw elevated errors but stabilized. No data leakage. Observability: dashboards and alerts tuned to avoid noise.

Raj: taking handoff. Thanks Alex. I'll keep watch for 2 hours and coordinate any further rollbacks/rollforwards.

Maya: thanks all. If we see re-emergence, plan B is temporary capacity bump for origin or selective cache sharding adjustment.

Sam (sre): leaving a note in postmortem checklist to evaluate prefetch heuristics and implement a safety cap for churny prefixes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigation complete (initial). Escalation closed. Please file postmortem and link incident-1745001234 in the PM.
